A backup is a single JSON file. It conta: A backup is a single JSON file. It contains your play history, your games, your notes, playthroughs, shelves, and app settings. Saved launch paths are not included; they stay on this PC.
By default, PlayCounter saves a backup o: By default, PlayCounter saves a backup once a week and keeps the last five. IGDB is a large public game database. Some of its entries record the name of the game's .exe file - bg3.exe for Baldur's Gate 3, for example. When it's there, PlayCounter finds the game right away.

Plenty of entries don't have it, though. That's the gap the Community database fills.

Set a hotkey that brings PlayCounter to: Set a hotkey that brings PlayCounter to the front from any app, one that shows your current session time in a small popup without leaving your game, and one that opens a note box for the session you're playing. Turn on Notes in game-start popups to pr: Turn on Notes in game-start popups to preview the active playthrough's note. Playthrough names is a separate switch. Choose Session saved, turn on Session notes in popups, and try the button. In the real popup it opens a small box for a note about that session; here it opens the sample journal. All three real preferences are independent and off by default.
When you start one of your own games, No: When you start one of your own games, Now Playing shows the note of its active playthrough. In Settings → Desktop popups, turn on Notes in game-start popups to see it in the popup as well. Turn on Session notes in popups to add a button to saved-session popups so you can write down what happened. Both options are off by default.
